{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1gyRZpLam6QQCwhRiv8","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Cholesky benchmark now runs distributed with MPI. It uses only `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt`, the executable name is unchanged, and it links `MPI::MPI_CXX` unconditionally. One trade-off: the `-r` hash matches the sequential source only when built with `-ffp-contract=off`, not with the default build flags (details below).\n\n**Design**\n- **Distribution:** rows are dealt cyclically across ranks, which balances the load. Each rank stores its rows column-major within the rank so the inner loops vectorize.\n- **Factorization:** left-looking, one column at a time. The owner of pivot row `j` finishes `L[j][j]` and broadcasts row `j`, then every rank updates its own rows below the diagonal.\n- **Generation and validation:** each rank replays the same `rand_r` stream but keeps only its own rows of B. Blocks of B circulate on a ring to build A. Validation uses the same ring pattern on L; the max reductions don't depend on order.\n- **Output:** `-r` gathers the full L to rank 0, which prints it as before. Timing is bracketed by barriers.\n\n**Verification**\n- **Equivalence:** 104 runs (n from 0 to 513, 1–16 ranks, `-v -r`) match the sequential reference exactly. Hash, samples, validation errors and exit codes are identical.\n- **Failure path:** I injected a non-positive-definite pivot into scratch copies of both programs. Both report the same element and fail the same way.\n- **Build:** I built out of tree in `/tmp`, so no artifacts were added to the project. The build has no warnings.\n\n**Decision for you: `-ffp-contract=off`**\n- **Why:** with default GCC contraction, the sequential build's rounding is inconsistent across code paths. At n=300 the default build hashes to `eef025eab9361974` and the contraction-off build to `7ee7181c03f3fd43`, so a reordered parallel version can't reproduce the default hash.\n- **Cost:** none measurable. At n=2048, one rank runs in 664 ms with it and 657 ms without. Sixteen ranks run in 110 ms and 109 ms.\n- **Effect:** if you compare hashes against the existing default-built binary, they will differ in the last bits. Say if you'd rather keep FMA and accept that.\n\n**Performance** (Cholesky phase only, 256-core host)\n\n| n | 1 rank | 16 ranks | 64 ranks |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 2048 | 664 ms (sequential original: 2139 ms) | 110 ms | 69–73 ms |\n| 4096 | 6.7 s | 0.66 s | ~0.4 s |\n\nScaling flattens at high rank counts because the algorithm needs one broadcast per column. I tried a lookahead version with nonblocking broadcasts. It was no faster under OpenMPI (it doesn't progress during compute), so I reverted to the simpler blocking version.\n\n**Not verified:** multi-node runs and other MPI implementations. Everything here ran on one host with OpenMPI. Also, the `-h` and unknown-option paths print usage from rank 0 only; `mpirun` adds its own abort notice on nonzero exits, which is normal.\n\n**Run it:** `mpirun -np 8 ./cholesky -n 2048 -v -r`\n\nI also saved a short memory note about the FMA finding and the OpenMPI progress behavior, for future work on this repo."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":820,"cache_read_input_tokens":173966,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":820},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"af2f8712-6388-4809-a11d-1ed97c3bb366","uuid":"2d80cfef-608b-45ba-b007-fae1ed771ac2","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:54:10.251Z","request_id":"req_011Cg1gyREE4KmyGG1suQN6y"}
